# Ezekiel 20 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

**2** And-the-word-of YHWH came to-me, saying:

**3** "Son-of man, speak to the-elders-of Israel and-say to-them, 'Thus says the-Lord YHWH: To-inquire-of-Me you [have]-come? As-I-live, I-will-not-be-inquired-of by-you,' declares the-Lord YHWH.

**4** "Will-you-judge-them, will-you-judge, son-of man? The-abominations-of their-fathers make-known to-them,

**5** and-say to-them, 'Thus says the-Lord YHWH: On-the-day I-chose Israel, and-I-lifted My-hand to-the-seed-of the-house-of Jacob, and-I-made-Myself-known to-them in-the-land-of Egypt, and-I-lifted My-hand to-them, saying, I [am] YHWH your-God —

**6** on-that day I-lifted My-hand to-them to-bring-them-out from-the-land-of Egypt to a-land which I-had-searched-out for-them, flowing [with]-milk and-honey — [the]-beauty she [is] of-all the-lands.

**7** And-I-said to-them, Each, the-detestable-things-of his-eyes, cast-away, and-with-the-idols-of Egypt do-not-defile-yourselves; I [am] YHWH your-God.

**8** But-they-rebelled against-Me and-were-not-willing to-listen to-Me; each the-detestable-things-of their-eyes they-did-not-cast-away, and-the-idols-of Egypt they-did-not-forsake. And-I-said to-pour-out My-fury upon-them, to-spend My-anger against-them in-the-midst-of the-land-of Egypt.

**9** But-I-acted for-the-sake-of My-name, that-it-should-not-be-profaned before-the-eyes-of the-nations in-whose-midst they [were], to-whom I-made-Myself-known before-their-eyes by-bringing-them-out from-the-land-of Egypt.

## EMET Literal Notes

- **20:9**: Va-e'eseh le-ma'an shemi — 'But I acted for the sake of My name.' Three times in this history (vv. 9, 14, 22) YHWH restrains His judgment to protect His reputation among the nations. His name-sake theology is a recurring theme.

- **20:25**: Chuqqot lo tovim — 'statutes not good.' One of the most difficult verses in Ezekiel. Possibly refers to the perversion of child sacrifice from the firstborn redemption law (Exod 22:28-29). God 'gave them over' to their own misreadings.

- **20:32-33**: Israel's desire to become 'like the nations' is flatly denied. YHWH will be their king whether they want Him or not — a sovereignty exercised through judgment.

— EMET
